bull.b: Extremely low leverage and a materially improved equity position give D‑Wave multi-quarter solvency and flexibility to fund R&D and commercialization. A strong balance sheet reduces near-term refinancing risk and supports multi-year investments in gate-model scaling and commercialization efforts.

A surge in bookings and a materially larger RPO/backlog provide durable revenue visibility versus prior quarters. With over half of RPO expected within 12 months and 71% within two years, the company has a clearer path to convert pipeline into recurring QCaaS, services and system revenues over the medium term.

bull.t: Strategic tech moves and government support
bull.b: The Quantum Circuits acquisition accelerates D‑Wave's gate-model roadmap, while prospective CHIPS Act funding and NSF/defense grants validate technology and supply‑chain support. These structural moves strengthen competitive positioning in superconducting gate systems and broaden addressable markets over years.

bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow at nearly $100M annualized implies continued reliance on existing liquidity or external funding. Even with improved FCF tracking to net loss, persistent cash burn constrains runway for scaling commercial operations and increases sensitivity to slower-than-expected bookings conversion.

bear.t: Revenue volatility and lumpy system sales
bear.b: Revenue is highly lumpy and dependent on occasional large system sales that can create sharp YoY swings, making quarter-to-quarter cash conversion and forecasting unreliable. This structural revenue concentration delays steady recurring revenue growth and complicates scaling sales, operations and margins sustainably.

Material increases in operating expenses driven by acquisition costs, hiring in sales/R&D, and noncash charges imply a heavier cost base ahead. If revenue growth lags, higher fixed and semi-fixed Opex will sustain large losses and delay achieving scalable margins despite long‑term commercial and tech progress.
